title: Use less, reuse more
description: Prevent waste before it reaches the bin.

content.intro: Recycling helps after we use something. Reusing an item can prevent waste before it starts.

facts.title: Use what you have
facts.body: A durable bottle or lunch container can be used many times. Start with something you already own.

facts.title: Make reuse a habit
facts.body: Bring your container home, wash it as directed, and pack it again.

facts.title: Care keeps things useful
facts.body: Store items carefully. Ask for help repairing damaged things instead of automatically replacing them.

content.question: Which habit can prevent a throwaway bottle each day?
choices: Use a new disposable bottle daily
Throw away a reusable bottle after one use
content.explanation: Refilling a clean reusable bottle lets you use the same item again instead of creating more waste.

title: Water-wise habits
description: Use the water you need without leaving it running.

content.intro: We need clean water for drinking and washing. Everyday habits can help us avoid wasting it.

facts.title: Pause the tap
facts.body: Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth. Turn it on when you need to rinse.

facts.title: Report a drip
facts.body: A dripping faucet can waste water over time. Tell an adult instead of trying to repair it yourself.

facts.title: Stay healthy
facts.body: Saving water does not mean skipping drinking or washing. Use what you need, then turn the tap off.

content.question: Which action saves water while brushing your teeth?
choices: Turn the tap off while brushing
content.explanation: Turning off the tap while brushing avoids running water you are not using.

title: Everyday energy
description: Spot simple ways to avoid wasting electricity.

content.intro: Lights and devices use energy. We can notice when they are useful and when they are not needed.

facts.title: Light the space you use
facts.body: When the last person leaves a room, turn off lights that are no longer needed.

facts.title: Choose efficient lighting
facts.body: LED bulbs use less electricity than traditional incandescent bulbs. An adult can choose and replace bulbs.

facts.title: Ask before switching
facts.body: Some equipment must stay on. Ask an adult before changing settings, and leave plugs and wires alone.

content.question: Everyone has left a room and its light is not needed. What helps?
choices: Leave the light on all day
content.explanation: Turning off an unneeded light avoids using electricity to light an empty room.

title: Food worth saving
description: Plan portions and ask for help saving leftovers.

source.title: EPA: Preventing wasted food at home

content.intro: Growing and preparing food takes resources. Planning what we use helps keep good food from becoming waste.

facts.title: Start with a portion
facts.body: Choose a serving you expect to eat. You can ask for more if you are still hungry.

facts.title: Save safely
facts.body: Ask an adult which leftovers can be saved and how to store them. Do not taste food to check its safety.

facts.title: Plan before buying
facts.body: Check which ingredients you already have before making a shopping list. This helps avoid buying too much.

content.question: Which choice helps avoid wasting food at lunch?
choices: Take extra food you do not want
Start with a serving and ask for more if hungry
content.explanation: Starting with a suitable serving helps avoid waste while leaving room to ask for more food.

title: Paper with a purpose
description: Make the most of paper before recycling it.

content.intro: Paper can be useful more than once. Using it carefully reduces the amount of new paper we need.

facts.title: Try the other side
facts.body: Use the blank back of a clean sheet for a draft or drawing. Ask before using someone else's paper.

facts.title: Share useful materials
facts.body: Keep books in good condition so other readers can use them. A classroom scrap-paper tray can collect reusable sheets.

facts.title: Recycle when finished
facts.body: When paper cannot be reused, check your local recycling rules. Keep it clean and separate from food.

content.question: A clean sheet has one blank side. How can you reuse it?
choices: Cover the blank side with food
content.explanation: Using the blank side gets another use from the same sheet before you need new paper.

title: Good neighbors to nature
description: Explore outdoors while respecting plants and wildlife.

source.title: National Park Service: Leave No Trace

content.intro: A park is a home for living things. We can enjoy exploring while leaving that home undisturbed.

facts.title: Watch from a distance
facts.body: Observe wildlife without chasing, touching, or feeding it. Take a photo or draw what you notice.

facts.title: Leave nature in place
facts.body: Leave flowers, rocks, and nests where they are. Other living things and visitors share this space.

facts.title: Follow the path
facts.body: Stay on marked paths with your group. Carry your own wrappers home if there is no bin.

content.question: You see flowers and insects beside a park path. What should you do?
choices: Pick the flowers and catch the insects
Watch quietly and leave them in place
content.explanation: Watching without disturbing plants or animals lets you learn while respecting their home.
